title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten sketch on the back of a Bourbaki 'Tribu n°59' typescript (Systèmes de racines). It belongs to the 1965 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' material. The handwriting is very abbreviated, and I read 'V' as Grothendieck's notation for a fibre functor (a 'realization', which he treats as a 'point').

The argument runs as follows.

1. Fibre functors and the motivic Galois group. Start from motives (the first line mentions classes of divisors, presumably the motive of a curve or abelian variety, or Néron–Severi). Given a fibre functor V to vector spaces over a field, the automorphisms of V on the category of motives form an algebraic group. This is the motivic Galois group as Aut^⊗(ω).

2. Many fibre functors. In general one must allow fibre functors with values in various coefficient fields. A Galois group acts on the set of fibre functors with values in k. Once one k-valued fibre functor is fixed, all the others are presumably torsors under its automorphism group. Two (or more) fibre functors thus give two or more algebraic groups Aut, which are inner forms of each other. This is exactly the gerbe/torsor picture of Tannakian categories.

3. Catalogue of 'points' (realizations) and their coefficient rings:
- ℓ-adic points: values in Z_ℓ or Q_ℓ.
- Transcendental (Betti) points: values in Q (the image letter may be R), 'voire Z', with '[structure supplémentaire]'. This presumably means Hodge structure and/or an integral lattice.
- A heuristic statement: such Betti fibre functors (with extra structure) should correspond bijectively to the points of X (the base) with values in C, modulo complex conjugation. In modern terms, the complex embeddings σ: k→C mod conjugation.
- Hodge–de Rham points: values in the base field(s), probably filtered/graded.
- Witt points: values in W_p(k). This is the crystalline realization over Witt vectors for a perfect field k of characteristic p.

The purpose is to set up the formalism of realizations as fibre functors on the Tannakian category of motives, and to classify these 'points' of the motivic gerbe.
errors: No outright mathematical errors are visible.

The suggested bijection between Betti fibre functors and complex points mod conjugation cannot hold for bare Q-valued fibre functors. Those form a torsor under the whole motivic Galois group, which is far more than the embeddings. It only makes sense with the 'structure supplémentaire' (Hodge structure, comparison data), which Grothendieck indeed adds in brackets.

The Betti and de Rham realizations attached to σ and σ̄ are identified via complex conjugation (F_∞). Hence 'mod conjugaison' is natural, but it identifies the functors only up to that isomorphism and a conjugation of the Hodge structure.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group as the automorphism group of a fibre functor on motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1960s), formalized by Saavedra Rivano 1972 and Deligne–Milne 1982
ideas.where_published: Récoltes et Semailles (description of the 'motivic Galois group'); Saavedra's thesis written under his direction

ideas.what: Galois action on the set of fibre functors; fibre functors form torsors; different fibre functors give inner-form groups
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian gerbe of fibre functors; torsor Isom^⊗(ω1,ω2)

ideas.what: Realizations viewed as 'points' with coefficient rings: ℓ-adic (Z_ℓ/Q_ℓ), Betti (Q, even Z), Hodge–de Rham, crystalline over W(k)
ideas.modern_name: Realization functors / fibre functors on motives; crystalline cohomology with W(k) coefficients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (standard conjectures era); crystalline: Grothendieck 1966–68, Berthelot 1974
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); Récoltes et Semailles

ideas.what: Betti fibre functors with supplementary structure should correspond bijectively to complex points (embeddings) of the base modulo complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Classification of 'Hodge/Betti points' of the motivic gerbe by complex embeddings; related to faithfulness of Hodge realization and recovering σ from realizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: No clear single source; spirit of Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles (1982)

missed.claim: The page suggests that 'transcendental points' (Betti fibre functors equipped with extra structure such as Hodge structure or an integral lattice) of the category of motives over a base X correspond bijectively to C-points of X modulo complex conjugation. This would be a kind of anabelian/section-type statement for the motivic gerbe. To my knowledge it was never formulated or pursued in this form.
missed.quote: Il suffit que un V correspondant biunivoquement aux pts de X à valeurs dans C, mod conjugaison
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It asks for an intrinsic characterization of the Betti realizations among all fibre functors, i.e. recovering complex embeddings from the Tannakian category plus extra structure. This is related to questions on reconstructing a field from its motives (cf. recent 'motivic anabelian' and Hodge-theoretic reconstruction results). The reading of the handwriting is, however, uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mostly an early (1965) sketch of the now-standard Tannakian picture of realizations as fibre functors/points, including the crystalline realization over Witt vectors, which was well known to come from Grothendieck. The only mildly unusual element is the conjectural bijection between Betti 'points' with extra structure and complex embeddings mod conjugation. It is too fragmentary and too uncertainly read to be striking.
transcription_corrections: 'Pts transcendants valeurs R' — the letter is likely Q (Betti with rational coefficients, 'voire Z'); uncertain.
'Il suffit que un V' may be 'Il semble que les V' (a conjecture rather than a sufficient condition).
'qui font les V de un groupe algébrique' likely means the automorphisms of V form ('font') an algebraic group.
'Aut Q' at the end is probably 'Aut ω' / 'Aut V' or 'Aut(Q)'; unclear.
'valeurs les généralisés' for Hodge–de Rham points likely refers to values in the base field(s) or in filtered/graded vector spaces; the superscript reads roughly 'corps de corps p' and is uncertain.
Line 2: 's'il y a un moyen' insertion is plausible; 'automorphismes des motifs' seems right.
